text: Thanks — I've started on this. I'll investigate why `Interval.fromISO` throws `Invalid DateTime` for date+duration strings when `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, fix it in the source, and verify against the existing test suite. ETA ~15 minutes.
Got it — I'll look into the `plus({ day: 61 })` result across the year-100 boundary (0099-12-31 → expected 0100-03-02) and fix it, verifying against the existing test suite. ETA ~20 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: `Interval.fromISO` parsed both halves with `DateTime.fromISO` first; for a date/duration string the duration half fails, and with `throwOnInvalid = true` that failure threw before the `Duration.fromISO` fallback could run. Now each `DateTime.fromISO` call is guarded so the duration fallback always runs. Both `"<date>/PT5H30M"` and `"PT5H30M/<date>"` now return the same valid interval as with the default setting. Verified with the full test suite (no new failures; the only 2 failures are pre-existing locale/ICU `toFormat` tests) plus targeted interval tests and a standalone repro.
On it — I'll dig into `isInDST` for the 1974 early-start case (America/Los_Angeles, 1974-01-06) and fix the underlying heuristic, verifying against the existing test suite. ETA ~20 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: `objToLocalTS()` in `src/impl/util.js` used `Date.UTC`, which maps years 0–99 to 1900–1999, then corrected the year with `setUTCFullYear(y - 1900)`. For 0099-12-31 + 61 days the day overflow was normalized against year 2000 (a leap year) before the year was rewritten, giving 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. Now the year/month/day are set directly with `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`, so normalization happens against year 99/100. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 }).toISODate()` now returns `"0100-03-02"`. Verified with a broad set of boundary cases (day/week/month/year arithmetic, leap-year checks for years 0/4/99/100/400/1900/2000) and the full test suite — no new failures (the only 2 failures are the pre-existing French `toFormat('FFF')`/`('FFFF')` ICU tests).

Got it — I'll investigate why `normalize()` yields `NaN` for mixed units like `{ years: 1, quarters: 2 }` and `{ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }`, fix the underlying conversion issue, and verify against the existing test suite. ETA ~20 minutes.

Understood — I'll fix the negative-year ISO formatting (`toISODate` returning `"00-1-01-01"` instead of `"-0001-01-01"`), which looks like the sign being counted in the zero-padding, and verify against the existing test suite. ETA ~20 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: the conversion matrices in `src/duration.js` (used by `normalize()`/`shiftTo()`/`as()` via `convert()`) were missing three entries — `casualMatrix.years.quarters`, `casualMatrix.quarters.seconds`, and `accurateMatrix.years.quarters` — so the lookup returned `undefined` and the value divided by `undefined` produced `NaN`. Added the three missing conversion factors. `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 2 }).normalize().toObject()` and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 2 }).normalize().toObject()` now return finite, correct numbers, and a scan of all unit pairs (9 units × many values, casual and longterm accuracy) shows no non-finite results. Full test suite unchanged: same 892 passing, only the 2 pre-existing French `toFormat` ICU failures.

Got it — I'll make `FixedOffsetZone` reject non-numeric offsets so `zone.isValid` is `false` and DateTimes using it are invalid with reason `"unsupported zone"`, checking existing zone tests don't rely on the current behavior. ETA ~20 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: `padStart()` in `src/impl/util.js` zero-padded the whole string including the leading minus sign, so `-1` became `"00-1"`. It now pads the absolute value to the requested width and re-attaches the sign, so `toISODate()` gives `-0001-01-01` and `-0010-01-01` (and `-0100`, `-1000`, `-10000` correctly), while positive years and other callers are unchanged. Verified across years -10000…10000 for `toISODate`/`toISO`/`toISOWeekDate`/`toFormat('yyyy')`, plus the full test suite — no new failures (only the 2 pre-existing French `toFormat` ICU failures).

Fixed. Root cause: `FixedOffsetZone`'s `isValid` getter was hard-coded to `return true`, so a zone built from a non-number offset looked valid; `DateTime` then only reported `"invalid input"` instead of `"unsupported zone"`. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid` is `false` and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone }).invalidReason` is `"unsupported zone"`. Numeric offsets (including 0 and negatives) and `FixedOffsetZone.instance`/`parseSpecifier` behavior are unchanged; all existing zone tests pass and the full suite shows no new failures.
